transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (NovaPay Dir Eng), Priya Singh (NovaPay ML Eng), Ethan Cole (NovaPay Infra), Jason Wu (NovaPay PM)

Summary: POC weekly sync - throughput optimizations, continuous batching, concurrency, queueing. Action items and next steps agreed.

[00:00:08] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call - Maya from Redwood, Arjun and Sofia on the call with me.
[00:00:15] Carlos: Hey, Carlos here, Priya and Ethan, Jason on mute.
[00:00:22] Maya: Cool, agenda is quick review of the benchmark we ran last week, dig into continuous batching params and then plan a short targeted run.
[00:00:30] Arjun: I'll kick off with numbers, we saw the sustained throughput at about 320 reqs/sec for the p50 payloads with avg 450 tokens, p95 latency drifted to 420ms during the 3x peak window. There was one anomaly around 10:12 where tail spiked to ~900ms, looks like a KV cache miss storm.
[00:01:02] Priya: Yeah we noticed that on our side too, there was a small cache eviction during the higher burst at 10:10, which coincided with a priority batch flush.
[00:01:14] Ethan: Just to flag, our infra has a short burst window where we allow queueing up to 200ms, beyond that we start dropping requests at the proxy level - is that something Redwood can accommodate?
[00:01:28] Sofia: Yes, we can configure transient queueing policies; the runtime supports soft queueing where we accept requests and backfill them into batches up to configured latency budget. We usually recommend 150-250ms for throughput-first workloads.
[00:01:45] Jason: Our product asks that tail latencies don't exceed 600ms more than 1% of the time, but for background features maybe we can tolerate slightly higher.
[00:01:58] Maya: Okay good. Arjun, can you walk through the batching config you tested?
[00:02:05] Arjun: Sure. Current run used continuous batching enabled, batch cap set to 12, dynamic batch flush threshold at 60ms, per-core concurrency of 4 streams. We also tested a higher cap at 16 which improved throughput to ~360 reqs/sec but increased p95 by ~30ms. The sweet spot seems to be 12-14 given NovaPay's average seq length.
[00:02:39] Carlos: When you say per-core concurrency 4, is that per-GPU worker? How would that translate if we move to Dedicated pool?
[00:02:47] Arjun: Good question. Per-worker stream concurrency maps to the number of simultaneous generation contexts per GPU shard. For Dedicated we can surface a concurrency map per-route so critical routes get lower concurrency (favor latency) and batch-friendly routes get higher concurrency (favor throughput).
[00:03:05] Priya: Our highest-volume route is /summarize which is very batch-friendly; /interactive-chat is low token but latency-sensitive.
[00:03:13] Sofia: Exactly, so the recommendation is to set /summarize to concurrency 8, batch cap 16, while /interactive-chat to concurrency 2, batch cap 8 and aggressive early flush.
[00:03:28] Maya: We also flagged the KV cache misses - Arjun, what mitigations did you try?
[00:03:33] Arjun: We enabled prefix caching and bumped memory allocation for the cache. That reduced repeated recompute on warm sessions. Also suggested adjusting sequence bucketing so similar-length requests are batched together; that reduced cache churn.
[00:03:48] Ethan: Bucketing sounds useful. We'll need to expose the seq-length distribution from our side so you can tune the buckets.
[00:03:54] Priya: We'll export the histogram from our telemetry, includes percentiles and peak hour breakdown.
[00:04:02] Maya: Great - Carlos, does NovaPay have concerns about transient queueing? You mentioned dropping beyond 200ms.
[00:04:09] Carlos: We prefer to avoid drops at the edge; short queueing is okay as long as it's controlled and we have visibility. Also we'd need to surface per-request retry hints if things cross thresholds.
[00:04:21] Arjun: We can instrument and expose queueing metrics and a flag that marks requests that were queued so you can correlate with upstream logs.
[00:04:30] Jason: That would be helpful.
[00:04:33] Maya: Alright, let's look at the anomalies - Arjun, can you show the dashboard? (screen share briefly)
[00:04:40] Arjun: On dashboard, here is p50/p95/p99, notice the KV miss cluster at 10:10 that lines up with a sudden increase in short-lived sessions. I think it's a pattern where a scheduled job did bursts of new conversations.
[00:04:58] Priya: That was a batch import job we ran in staging, sorry that slipped into the flap. In prod we don't have those scheduled spikes but our traffic can be spiky during payroll windows.
[00:05:09] Maya: Important to test with representative traffic - Carlos, can you share the sample histogram?
[00:05:14] Carlos: Yes we'll send it after the call.
[00:05:18] Arjun: For the next run I propose: continuous batching on, batch cap 16 for batch-friendly routes, dynamic flush 60ms, concurrency per-route as Sofia suggested (8 for summaries, 2 for chat), and target concurrent load of 500-800 sessions to stress queuing.
[00:05:36] Ethan: If we do 800 concurrent what do you expect for p95?
[00:05:40] Arjun: From prior sims, with those settings and proper caching, p95 should be under 450ms for batch-friendly flows; chat might be 300-400ms if we keep concurrency low. Worst-case tail events could spike higher if there's a cache miss storm.
[00:05:56] Priya: Is there an easy knob to throttle at ingress if queue starts growing?
[00:06:01] Sofia: Yes we can set soft backpressure thresholds and graceful rate limiters per route; they return warning headers and can be adjusted per environment.
[00:06:09] Jason: We need those headers for telemetry.
[00:06:12] Maya: Noted. Okay next, capacity planning for Dedicated - Carlos earlier asked about mapping.
[00:06:19] Arjun: We'll provide a recommended concurrency map with expected RPS per pool. For example, a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with the tuned config handled about 1.2k effective RPS for summarize when batching caps are high, but that assumes sustained batch formation and warm KV cache. If you have many short sessions the effective RPS drops.
[00:06:41] Carlos: Good, can you provide the per-route numbers so we can model costs?
[00:06:45] Arjun: Yes, we'll deliver a spreadsheet showing expected throughput and latency per config.
[00:06:50] Priya: Did you try quantization? I remember a note about q4 variants that speed up perf.
[00:06:56] Arjun: We tested a q4f16-like profile in staging; it reduced GPU memory and slightly improved batch throughput but introduced a small quality delta which your team should validate. For this pilot we recommend the float16 baseline for quality parity, then consider q4 for cost-optimization after eval.
[00:07:13] Carlos: We'll want a small eval set before dropping precision.
[00:07:18] Maya: Absolutely. Okay back to tests - agreed that we run a targeted 1-hour load with the tuned params. Arjun and Maya will run it from Redwood side, NovaPay will provide traffic shape and let us know peak windows to simulate.
[00:07:31] Arjun: One more note: during the last run the scheduler occasionally formed very large batches (20+) which caused token spikes and pushed latency for interactive routes. We recommend capping at 16 and setting per-route caps to avoid that.
[00:07:45] Ethan: Ok we'll map routes to policies in the next week.
[00:07:50] Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
[00:07:54] Priya: We just need the dashboards and the data to validate quality after the quantized run if we do it.
[00:08:00] Maya: We'll share the perf dashboards and the raw CSVs.
[00:08:03] Carlos: On security/compliance side, procurement asked if the Dedicated pool can have VPC peering and KMS integration - is that supported?
[00:08:11] Sofia: Yes Dedicated supports customer VPC peering for private deployments and integrates with KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We'll attach the security brief and SOC2 excerpt after the call.
[00:08:23] Jason: That helps.
[00:08:26] Maya: Ok, recap and next steps: Redwood to run 1-hour targeted test and share metrics, NovaPay to send traffic histogram, Redwood to provide concurrency map spreadsheet and security brief. We'll reconvene next week to review.
[00:08:40] Carlos: Sounds good.
[00:08:42] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the review.
[00:08:47] (crosstalk and brief goodbyes)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription has a few misheard technical terms (q4 variants transcribed as q-four, some proper nouns mangled), speaker overlaps around sign-off.

End of transcript.
